subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Desalination: Turning Seawater Into Fresh Water
description: A fast breakdown of Desalination: Turning Seawater Into Fresh Water for builders.

hook.text: 97% of Earth's water is saltwater. Desalination can turn it fresh, but it takes enormous amounts of energy.

buildup.text: Reverse osmosis pushes seawater through membranes with pores so tiny that salt can't pass. Only water molecules get through.

discovery.text: Early desalination used distillation — boiling water and collecting steam. Reverse osmosis uses 75% less energy than distillation.

twist.text: Brine — the concentrated salt left over — damages marine ecosystems. One gallon of fresh water creates 1.5 gallons of brine.

climax.text: Israel now gets 80% of its domestic water from desalination. It transformed a water-scarce nation into one with a surplus.

punchline.text: Push seawater through a membrane. Catch the fresh. Dispose of the salt.

quiz.question: What environmental problem does desalination create?
options: The noise from desalination plants disrupts marine animal communication
Brine discharge — concentrated salt waste — damages marine ecosystems
Desalination removes too much water from the ocean, lowering sea levels
